rows: Why can't you just dissolve indigo in water and dye cloth?
Indigotin is insoluble. Must reduce to leucoindigo (soluble) → dye fabric → reoxidize to insoluble indigotin inside the fiber
Why do woad and tropical indigo produce the same color?
Same molecule: indigotin. Different plants, identical compound. Tropical plant has 10× concentration.
Using iron mordant to darken/cool a color — "sadden" the bright mordant-alum result
Organic dye precipitated onto Al(OH)₃ (or similar) substrate → insoluble colored particle usable in oil/tempera
What destroyed the madder industry in 1869?
Simultaneous synthesis of alizarin (madder's active compound) by Perkin and Graebe/Liebermann — immediate price collapse
What destroyed the natural indigo industry?
BASF's industrial synthetic indigo (1897, Heumann synthesis) — price dropped 20:1 within a decade
High-quality red using madder + aluminum mordant + oil treatment — developed in India, premium washfast red
Why are most lake pigments fugitive?
The organic chromophore (the actual dye molecule) is still present and still absorbs UV → still photodegrades; the alumina substrate doesn't protect it
